competences: The learner identifies the term's source-grounded facts about term revision 1: uganda as an independent nation, the government of uganda, population, size and distribution.
The learner answers questions about Mixed revision of the term correctly.
languageCompetence: Reads and spells words associated with independence, national, democracy, citizenship.
objectives: By the end of the period, learners should be able to identify the sourced facts about term revision 1: uganda as an independent nation, the government of uganda, population, size and distribution.
By the end of the period, learners should be able to answer the available original questions on Mixed revision of the term.
priorKnowledge: Learners have studied SST topics about independent Uganda, the government and population during this term. They use their earlier notes while reviewing term revision 1: uganda as an independent nation, the government of uganda, population, size and distribution.
materials: SST revision chart on term revision 1: uganda as an independent nation, the government of uganda, population, size and distribution
P5 SST reference notes and original exercise questions
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher introduces term revision 1: uganda as an independent nation, the government of uganda, population, size and distribution and reviews relevant earlier Primary Five work. They ask "Who composed the Uganda national anthem?" and connect the replies with the original source material.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall prior SST knowledge, answer the opening question and identify the earlier topics that relate to the new work.

steps.content: The meaning of independence Independence is when a country is free from foreign political, social and economic influence. Uganda got her independence on Monday 9 th October 1962. The National Anthem of Uganda was first officially sung on 9 th October 1962 It is the national anthem Peter G. Wingard State the anthem which was used before Uganda got her independence. The British national anthem At the opening of any function of national importance. Messages of the National Anthem To remind people about the fertile soil and favorable climate of Uganda. Respect for the National Anthem To remind us f our national duties It shows national unity To express the national beliefs of the nation To show national identify Apart from the national anthem, outline two other attributes of a nation.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes and explains the source-grounded facts on term revision 1: uganda as an independent nation, the government of uganda, population, size and distribution, starting with "The meaning of independence; Independence is when a country is free from foreign political, social and economic influence.". They ask learners to explain the stated information and relate it to the current revision topic.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the original content, respond to teacher questions, identify relevant facts and copy or correct their revision notes.

steps.content: Who composed the Uganda national anthem? | Who assisted George William Kakoma to compose the national anthem? | When and how the stanzas of the national anthem are sung? | Give two reasons why Ugandans sing the national anthem | When was the national anthem played for the first time in Uganda?
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher sets the original questions, including "Who composed the Uganda national anthem?" and "Who assisted George William Kakoma to compose the national anthem?". They monitor answers, support learners who need help and correct responses using the accepted source pack.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise independently, explain their reasoning and correct any answers that do not match the factual notes.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher summarises term revision 1: uganda as an independent nation, the government of uganda, population, size and distribution using the recorded facts, then checks understanding with "Who composed the Uganda national anthem?". They ask "Who assisted George William Kakoma to compose the national anthem?" and allocate remaining questions for further revision.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the concluding oral questions, mention one useful fact and complete corrections in their exercise books.

assessment: Use the original questions "Who composed the Uganda national anthem?" and "Who assisted George William Kakoma to compose the national anthem?", with the remaining sourced exercise, to check individual learners' understanding. Mark against the source facts.
homework: Revise and complete the remaining original questions including "Give one way school children express the spirit of nationalism when on assemblies."
